name: COUP D'ETAT
description: Compendium game with six different hands per round: Barbu, Waterloo, Siege, Touche, Guillotine, and Dominos. The Director (dealer) chooses which hand to play; players pay penalties to the Director. The holder of the Coup card may try to overthrow the Director by achieving the hand objective; success makes them Director. Winner is the player with the most money after a number of rounds equal to the number of players.

content.text: Compendium game with six different hands per round: Barbu, Waterloo, Siege, Touche, Guillotine, and Dominos. The Director (dealer) chooses which hand to play; players pay penalties to the Director. The holder of the Coup card may try to overthrow the Director by achieving the hand objective; success makes them Director. Winner is the player with the most money after a number of rounds equal to the number of players.

Believed to have been first played by political prisoners in France over two centuries ago. Published in 1966 by Parker Brothers; the basic game is related to the traditional French game Barbu, with the Coup and Hidden Coup mechanics likely an American addition.
Two to six players; each plays for himself; partnerships not permitted. For three players, remove sevens and eights from the deck.
Standard 32-card pack (eight cards per suit: Ace, 10, King, Queen, Jack, 9, 8, 7) plus one special Coup card. Suits are Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs; Ace is highest, then 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7.
32-card deck (or standard 52 with agreed stripping), optional Coup card or designated wild card; play money in francs (e.g. 10,000 per player).
Director shuffles and deals eight cards face down to each player and places one card face down in the center. If the center card is the Coup card, Director shuffles and deals again.

items.text: Short Game: Eliminate Barbu and Touche entirely. Each round consists of three of the four remaining hands (Waterloo, Siege, Guillotine, Dominos). As soon as three hands have been completed the Directorship passes to the next player. All other rules remain the same.
